title: Split the runners config: execution tables to ticfac, tracker tables stay
description:
Cut the runners config in two. This is the hardest tick in the epic and the one
that decides whether orchestration config is TRULY extracted.

`internal/herd/config` is ~8016 lines and is genuinely MIXED. One struct carries
both domains (config/types.go:153): the execution side reaches Orchestrator,
Orchestration, Role, TierVariant, Environment, Sandbox; the tracker side reaches
Signals (:291), SignalSource (:311), Sweep (:343). One parser (load.go) and one
migrator (migrate.go), 1246 lines together, treat the file as a SINGLE VERSIONED
DOCUMENT.

Three compounding difficulties:
1. The shared struct — there is no seam inside the type today.
2. `internal/sandbox` already depends on 21 exported identifiers from this
   package across six files (LoadRepo, DecideOverride, ProbeSocket, Worker,
   Tier and more), and sandbox is NOT part of this move.
3. The migrator versions the whole document as one unit, so a split has to
   decide who owns the version and what happens to a file written by the other
   side's migrator.

Do:
- Decide and log WHO PARSES `.tick/runners.toml`. The options are genuinely
  different, and the decision outlives this tick: one parser in ticks that ticfac
  reaches through `tk --json`; two readers over one file, each pinned to its own
  tables (today's shape, made honest); or two files. Weigh it against the
  standing rule that ticfac talks to ticks only via `tk --json` and a pinned
  bundle — today's direct read is a second coupling that a second substrate
  multiplies.
- Whatever is chosen, the execution tables (orchestrator, orchestration, roles,
  tiers, environment) must be ticfac's, and the tracker tables (signals, signal
  sources, sweeps) must stay ticks'.
- Resolve the sandbox dependency explicitly. Do NOT strand it: either sandbox
  moves with the execution half, or the identifiers it needs get a home that
  survives the split. Say which, and why, in the RESULT file.
- Migration must not corrupt an existing file written by the old single
  migrator.
notes:
2026-09-10 13:12 - runner-state: first spawn attempt ABORTED and torn down by hand. My shell wrapper timed out at 2 minutes and killed tk herd spawn AFTER herdr had created the workspace, worktree, branch and a live pi agent, but BEFORE tk wrote .tick/logs/herd/av8/wgi.json. That left a live worker with no manifest — no durable pointer from the tick to the workspace — which is exactly the orphan shape tick 5hz describes, produced here by an interrupted dispatch rather than an interrupted teardown. The agent had received no prompt (0.0% context), so nothing was lost. Workspace wPQ closed, worktree and branch removed by hand because tk herd cleanup needs a manifest and there was none.
2026-09-10 13:14 - runner-state: dispatched on pi/cloudflare GLM-5.3 effort=high (default tier) from base a085b31
--- merged from remote ---
2026-09-10 17:13 - decision: Which TOML decoder does ticfac's execution-half reader use? → github.com/BurntSushi/toml v1.6.0 — the same decoder and version ticks' reader uses — ticfac's go.mod was dependency-free and Go stdlib-first is the standing rule, but a hand-rolled TOML subset is exactly what this tick retires: the format carries inline tables, arrays of tables, escaping and a version gate whose 'present vs omitted' semantics need real decode metadata (toml.MetaData.IsDefined/Undecoded). BurntSushi/toml is the decoder ticks' own reader is written against, already in the shared module cache, zero further deps — and pinning the same version keeps the two readers comparable line by line, which is the whole point of the split's shared half. [class:library-choice]
acceptance_criteria: A logged decision names who parses .tick/runners.toml and why, weighed against the tk --json + pinned-bundle rule; execution tables are ticfac's and tracker tables are ticks'; internal/sandbox is not stranded and the RESULT file says where its 21 identifiers live; an existing file written by the old single migrator still loads correctly in both projects, covered by a test; go test -short -timeout 45m ./... green.
closed_reason: Split the runners config: the execution half moved to ticfac with its own internal/herd/config, plus a version test and a refusal test for an unlaunchable runner. It logged the decision its acceptance required about who parses .tick/runners.toml. Deviation noted and corrected at integration: it committed RESULT-wgi.md onto its branch; archived and removed. Wave gate green (EXIT=0, reconcile 710s).
